authorityRules.canonicalState: One immutable structured Product Graph revision document is authoritative per revision.
authorityRules.derivedState: Normalized relational rows, indexes, caches, and other projections are non-authoritative and must be regenerable from an identified canonical revision.

criteria.deterministicDiff: Both are deterministic; structured snapshots preserve directly inspectable canonical revision state.
criteria.mergeability: Normalized rows have narrower logical units, but V1 conflict resolution belongs to immutable graph-delta/revision semantics rather than direct canonical row mutation.
criteria.migrationVersioning: Structured schema-versioned revisions minimize the authoritative migration surface; derived projections can be rebuilt.
criteria.sliceQueryErgonomics: Structured state supports deterministic slices after hydration; derived indexes/projections are permitted when workload evidence requires partial reads.
criteria.testability: Both qualify; structured canonical fixtures make whole-revision equality and reconstruction direct.
criteria.humanInspectability: Structured canonical state exposes the semantic whole without projection.
criteria.performance: Only deterministic storage-surface evidence is accepted; structured serialization is smaller on both qualified fixtures and no latency claim is made.

unmeasured: Production database latency and indexing behavior at realistic project sizes.
Migration cadence and operational cost as later P02 semantics expand.
revisitTriggers: Realistic Product Graph workloads miss explicit hydration, memory, or slice/query budgets.
Derived projection regeneration or freshness cannot satisfy recovery/query requirements.
Observed graph-delta concurrency evidence identifies immutable-revision persistence as the bottleneck.
Whole-revision migration transforms become unsafe or operationally unacceptable.
A required transactional partial-update workflow cannot be represented safely as a new immutable Product Revision.
